official.deadline_note: Two windows in the same round for new and renewal applications for support starting from the autumn semester 2027: 01.12.2026 (notification end of February 2027, payment beginning of March 2027) and 15.02.2027 (notification beginning of April 2027, payment beginning of April 2027). The 15.07.2026 and 15.09.2026 windows for Autumn 26 / Spring 27 support have passed.
official.application_cycle: 2026-2027 academic year (Application form 2026-2027); requests for support starting from the autumn semester 2027
official.status_note: EPFL lists open deadlines for support starting from the autumn semester 2027 (01.12.2026 and 15.02.2027, new and renewal applications) and states that applications for scholarships for the 2025-2026 academic year are now closed.
official.tuition_coverage_note: EPFL publishes no tuition coverage for the Hans Wilsdorf fund; the support is a means-tested monthly grant whose amount is calculated from the student's social, family and financial situation and budget, including rent.
benefits: Support paid for 5 months per semester, up to a maximum of ten months per year of study
Payment at the start of each semester
Renewable each academic year by submitting a complete application again, if the financial situation still warrants it
Maximum monthly scholarship of up to 2'600 CHF, the amount determined by the social, family and financial situation of the student and of the persons in charge of support
eligibility: International students: as of the successful completion of the first year cycle and after spending at least one year at EPFL, and living in the canton of Geneva

Students with Swiss nationality, C permit holder, refugee or Swiss secondary education certificate: as of the CMS, and living in the canton of Geneva or who have applied for a scholarship from the cantonal scholarship office of the canton of Geneva (SBPE)
Be in a difficult financial situation, on the same criteria as the EPFL social scholarship
Subsidiarity: the scholarship is a last resort, once all other possibilities (parental contribution, state grants, loans and loan proposals) have been rejected

International students must be experiencing an unexpected and sudden change in their social, family or financial situation, since funding for the entirety of studies must be secured before joining EPFL

Meet the same criteria as the EPFL social scholarship

Inform EPFL of any change in social, family or financial situation likely to affect the scholarship granted

All documents listed on the application form (EPFL: all the documentation required for the application is listed on the form)
For students who applied to the Geneva cantonal scholarship office (SBPE), the acknowledgement of receipt of that application
selection_criteria: Financial need assessed on the social, family and financial situation of the student and of the persons in charge of support
Last-resort (subsidiarity) principle applied to every other source of funding
For international students, evidence of an unexpected and sudden change in circumstances
Decisions taken by the Social Commission (EPFL staff and teaching staff plus a student representative), which meets 5 or 6 times a year
coverage: Means-tested monthly grant calculated from the student's budget, including rent
5 months per semester, a maximum of ten months per year of study

Complete the form and attach every document it lists
Submit before one of the two deadlines of the round
official.application_route: Download the EPFL Application form 2026-2027, tick the "Hans Wilsdorf scholarship" box, and submit the completed form with all listed documents to EPFL by the round deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Swiss nationals, C permit holders, refugees and holders of a Swiss secondary education certificate who live in the canton of Geneva or who have applied to the Geneva cantonal scholarship office (SBPE); international students must live in the canton of Geneva
official.international_eligibility: Yes, but only after at least one year at EPFL and successful completion of the first-year cycle, and only when living in the canton of Geneva
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field-of-study restriction; the fund is restricted to students living in the canton of Geneva or who have applied to the Geneva cantonal scholarship office (SBPE)
official.duration: Per academic year (1 or 2 semesters), that means 5 months per semester and a maximum of ten months per year of study
official.description: The Hans Wilsdorf Foundation fund is a private foundation fund administered by EPFL for students from Geneva in financial difficulty. EPFL manages it according to the same criteria as the EPFL social scholarship and pays the support at the start of each semester, for five months per semester and up to ten months per year of study.
official.program_type: Need-based scholarship from a private foundation, administered by EPFL

applicant_utility.summary: This is an internal EPFL safety net, not an admission scholarship: you have to be enrolled at EPFL and resident in the canton of Geneva before it can help you at all. The money arrives as a means-tested monthly grant of up to CHF 2,600, paid in one go at the start of each semester, so what actually moves the decision is documented evidence of a real budget shortfall rather than any academic merit. Because EPFL treats it as a last resort, your SBPE (Geneva cantonal) application and every other funding source must already be exhausted or formally in progress, and anything later awarded by the canton has to be paid back to EPFL.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled EPFL bachelor's or master's students living in Geneva whose finances have genuinely deteriorated and who have already lodged an SBPE application.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are resident in the canton of Geneva; students living in Vaud or elsewhere cannot use this fund and must apply for the EPFL social scholarship instead
File your SBPE (Geneva cantonal scholarship office) application first and keep the acknowledgement of receipt, which must be attached to the EPFL file
Download the current-year 2-in-1 Application form 2026-2027 rather than reusing last year's file, and check that the "Hans Wilsdorf scholarship" box is actually ticked
Assemble the full document list printed on the form beforehand - EPFL warns that the form and documents take time and that supplementary documents may be requested during processing
Send the signed lease as soon as you have accommodation, because without it the grant is calculated with no rent at all
International applicants: verify you have completed a full year at EPFL and passed the first-year cycle before the deadline you are targeting
common_rejection_risks: Applying through the EPFL social scholarship form without ticking the Hans Wilsdorf box, which routes a Geneva-resident file to the wrong fund
No SBPE application on file for Swiss nationals and C permit holders, or no acknowledgement of receipt attached, which breaks the subsidiarity test
International applicants who apply before completing one year at EPFL and the first-year cycle
Presenting a foreseeable change (a sibling starting university, parental retirement at legal age, or simply poor budget planning) instead of an unexpected and sudden deterioration
Submitting at the very last window of the round, so the Social Commission runs out of meeting dates before the notification date EPFL publishes
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and compulsory semester fees remain the applicant's responsibility: CHF 780 per semester invoice (CHF 730 tuition, CHF 25 AGEPoly, CHF 16 sports facilities, CHF 9 social fund), and CHF 2,240 per semester for foreign students newly subject to the tripled tuition fee from the fall semester 2025. Health insurance, travel to and from Switzerland, installation costs and the uncovered months of the year are also not funded by this grant.
document_audit: The form is a single 2-in-1 document covering new and renewal requests - use the 2026-2027 version, not an older file
The fund-specific tick box is the only thing that distinguishes this application from a plain EPFL social scholarship request
Parents' income documents are still required even for applicants over 25, unless exceptional circumstances are argued and documented
If the chosen deadline's notification falls late, payment also falls late, so plan the first months of the semester without the grant
alerts: There are only two entry points per round (01.12.2026 and 15.02.2027 for support starting autumn semester 2027); miss both and you wait for the next cycle
Repayment trap: if the canton or state later awards you a grant or loan, EPFL will ask for partial or total reimbursement - there is no double financing
Geographic trap: the fund follows Geneva residency, so a move out of the canton or a change of SBPE canton changes which fund you should be applying to
International students must have secured funding for the whole of their studies before arriving at EPFL; hardship caused by under-budgeting is explicitly excluded
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the downloadable EPFL Application form 2026-2027 with the Hans Wilsdorf box ticked, attach the form's full document list plus the SBPE acknowledgement, and send it to EPFL before the deadline; the Social Commission then reviews the file and payment follows at the start of the semester.
